tags: why do dogs look at you when they poop
script: It's a moment every dog owner has noticed. Your dog heads to the perfect spot, squats, and then looks straight at you. It feels awkward, but it actually makes a lot of sense. In the wild, dogs are at their most vulnerable while they're going to the bathroom, since they can't run or defend themselves easily. So they likely look to the most trusted member of their pack to keep watch. By making eye contact, your dog is checking that you're there, that everything is okay, and that you've got their back. It's less about privacy and more about security. Some dogs also simply look at you out of habit, or because they've learned you often reward them with praise after they finish. It's generally best to stay calm, stay nearby and let them do their business without rushing. Praising right after is a great way to reinforce good potty habits, too. If your dog seems unusually anxious while going, strains, or has changes in stools, mention it to your vet. Otherwise, take it as a compliment. Your dog trusts you enough to guard their most vulnerable moment.
